# the contributor audit: selected critical circuits and finite response menus

Regularity precision from Defect's independent audit: regularity here means differentiability of the mass in the full hyperplane parameters (A,b), with the usual coarea derivative. Differentiability only along normals constrained through the original source is not enough by itself for the reuse at a different boundary source. The concrete proper/strictly-full/strictly-empty condition is sufficient. The source is being clarified to adopt the full-parameter premise; every PASS below is under that premise.

Source: `candidate b1ef83513bdb0bcf`, Sections 1--4, together with the strict-contact argument in `candidate 567aa083fc8ee3ab`. Independent root audit: PASS within the explicitly stated regular, full-fiber hypotheses. This is not a proof of OC or of general selected-circuit efficiency.

For a regular critical cap through Y with nonzero continuous normal u and positive total coarea, differentiating the full ambient normal gives the mixed section centroid exactly Y. A second deepest point strictly inside the cap can be retained while the threshold is increased and positive mass is removed. A distinct second deepest point on the boundary gives a strictly negative normal derivative through that second point. Thus every distinct deepest point is strictly outside this regular cap. This argument requires positive total coarea, not a proper cut in the source fiber specifically. The source's differentiability premise supplies the first variation, so supporting-facet jumps have not been discarded.

For a finite common linear symmetry group with zero average, its inverse group also has zero average. Its determinant has absolute value one, because each element has finite order. Fiber invariance therefore puts each fiber centroid at the common fixed point zero. If centers form the affine graph c(z), the maps (z,x) -> (z,c(z)+G(x-c(z))) are actual invertible affine maps, preserve the integer base, and preserve fiber volume. The transformed halfspaces have continuous normals G^{-T}u and the same base tilt in centered shear coordinates. No claim of unit-normal or boundary-area preservation is needed.

Quasiconcavity of extended halfspace depth follows directly: a halfspace containing a convex combination contains one of its summands. Averaging a deepest point's orbit therefore gives the fiber centroid as another deepest point. If the original point has a regular positive continuous-normal circuit, strict contact and positive balance forbid a different deepest point in the same fiber. Thus the selected source is the actual fiber centroid, not an external rounded centroid.

The orbit of one actual regular critical cap is again critical and its continuous normals positively balance. Caratheodory gives a subcircuit of at most d+1 rows, after deleting zero coefficients. A vertex maximizing the common base tilt can be exposed individually because the base set is finite. At that fiber every orbit cap contains its corresponding through-centroid cap.

For each fixed unit normal n, [n dot (x-c(z))+B ell(z)]_+ is a nonnegative convex function of the physical variables; affinity of c is essential. B is finite because all fibers are bounded and the finitely many other bases have strictly negative ell. On the selected fiber boundary the value is the nonnegative radial flux; it vanishes on all other boundary fibers. Its denominator is d times that fiber's volume. The through-centroid cut has zero cut-plane radial flux, so its boundary integral is d times its cap volume. Inclusion and nonnegativity, not a false offset-cap flux identity, give the Gamma bound for every row and every normalized nonnegative weight choice. The d=1 endpoint interpretation is valid. No d=0 boundary measure is asserted.

For a finite regular menu, S_j is the scalar threshold derivative and b_j=S_j u_j. Positive rescaling of the defining cap equation multiplies u_j and divides S_j by the same factor, leaving b_j fixed. The equations theta_j proportional to rho_j/S_j and rho_j=theta_j S_j establish the claimed equivalence between response weights and continuous-normal balances. The feasible weight set is a compact polytope. A dependence among more than rank(1,b_j) positive columns permits both signed small perturbations, proving the extreme-support bound. There are finitely many extremes, so the finite maximum commutes with the potential supremum without attainment. The displayed dual is the usual finite feasible bounded LP dual, with no unproved potential minimax exchange.

The nonnegative summation of epsilon-good potentials is valid for fixed finitely many chosen source profiles. It does not prove that such potentials exist for arbitrary fibers, that all competing profiles pay, or that a variational minimum has the required regularity and supporting-facet allocations. Those missing interfaces remain explicit.

Consequently the exact R4 and primitive-simplex prescribed-profile obstructions remain valid, but do not refute the existential selected-circuit assertion. Their product symmetries explicitly produce a different paying circuit. This quantifier correction is mathematically essential.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
